65% OF NEW GCC JOBS IN INDIA REQUIRE AI SKILLS. THE FUTURE OF WORK IS ALREADY CHANGING. A new report by ANSR, Talent Trends in GCCs in India 2026, carries an important message for India’s students, professionals, educators and employers. 📊 Here are the numbers we cannot afford to ignore: 🔹 Nearly 65% of new GCC roles created in 2026 require AI skills. 🔹 Demand for AI and data professionals has increased by approximately 45% year-on-year. 🔹 GCC hiring grew by around 12–15% year-on-year in the first half of 2026. 🔹 Postings for emerging roles, including Forward Deployed Engineers and AI engineers, have surged dramatically. Source: ANSR, Talent Trends in GCCs in India 2026. But the most important takeaway is not just about the numbers. It is about how we prepare for the jobs of tomorrow. AI is no longer relevant only to computer science graduates. A finance professional who understands AI-powered analytics. A software engineer who can build AI-enabled applications. A cybersecurity specialist who can use intelligent threat detection. A business graduate who can automate workflows and interpret data. Each represents a different way to combine domain expertise with AI capabilities. What does this mean for India’s youth? 1. Learn AI by applying it. Move beyond merely using AI tools. Learn how to solve real problems with them. 2. Combine AI with a domain. AI + Finance. AI + Marketing. AI + Education. AI + Healthcare. AI + Cybersecurity. Your existing knowledge can become more valuable when complemented by AI skills. 3. Build demonstrable capabilities. Projects, portfolios, practical assignments and measurable outcomes can help demonstrate what you can actually do. 4. Develop human skills alongside technical skills. Critical thinking, communication, creativity, ethical judgement and problem-solving remain essential to translating technology into business value. And what does this mean for educational institutions? We must rethink the relationship between education and employability. AI literacy, data fluency, industry projects and experiential learning should not remain optional additions to the curriculum. They must become an integral part of preparing students for a rapidly evolving workplace. It will be realised by people who know how to use technology intelligently. The question for every student, professional and institution is simple: Are we preparing for the jobs that existed yesterday—or developing the capabilities that the world will need tomorrow? The future of employability will belong to those who combine knowledge, skills, adaptability and the ability to work intelligently with AI. #ArtificialIntelligence #FutureOfWork #IndiaJobs #GlobalCapabilityCentres #Upskilling #DigitalSkills #Employability #Education #SkillDevelopment
Chandra Shekhar yadav 8mo Report this post AI SUMMIT 2026- India 5 Burning issues to be discussed 1. Sovereign AI and Democratizing Compute For many nations, the focus has shifted from "using AI" to "owning AI." Sovereign Infrastructure: Discussing how countries can build their own data centers and compute stacks to avoid total dependence on a few global tech giants. The AI Divide: Creating a framework for the "Global South" to access high-level compute resources so the gap between AI-rich and AI-poor nations doesn't become permanent. 2. Global Governance & The "Leaders’ Declaration" With the EU AI Act in full force by 2026, a major goal of this summit would be Interoperability. Unified Safety Standards: Reaching a consensus on what constitutes "unacceptable risk" (e.g., autonomous weaponry or biometric social scoring). The Leaders' Declaration: Signing a formal treaty to ensure that AI development remains human-centric and follows common safety protocols across borders. 3. Human Capital & The "Great Reskilling" As AI agents begin to own "outcomes" rather than just "tasks," the labor market is in flux. Skill-Based vs. Degree-Based Hiring: Addressing the 2026 trend where specific AI skills often command higher market value than traditional degrees. Universal Basic Services/Income: High-level talks on social safety nets for sectors most disrupted by automation (e.g., administrative, legal, and customer service roles). 4. AI for "Planet" (Sustainability) The massive energy requirements of AI training models are now a climate priority. Energy-Efficient AI: Mandating "green" training protocols and sharing technologies that reduce the carbon footprint of massive GPU clusters. Climate Resilience: Using AI to predict and mitigate the effects of climate change, specifically for agriculture in developing nations. 5. Security & Information Integrity In a world of hyper-realistic deepfakes, "Truth" is a matter of national security. Content Provenance: Standardizing "watermarking" for all AI-generated content to prevent election interference and social engineering. Chandra Shekhar yadav 8mo Report this post India’s Talent Crisis Is Not a Hiring Problem. It’s a Learning Emergency. “82% employers can’t find the right talent.” Let that sink in. According to a recent report covered by The Economic Times, India ranks among the most talent-constrained markets globally — at 82%. The global average is 72%. Pause. This is not a statistic. This is a structural alarm bell. Degrees Are Increasing. Employability Is Shrinking. Every year, India produces lakhs of graduates. Engineering. BCA.BBA.MBA.BA.BSc. Yet companies say: “We are not getting the right person.” This is not hypocrisy. This is a skills architecture failure. We built an education system optimized for examinations. The market rewards execution. We trained memory. Industry needs mastery. The Brutal Reality No One Wants to Admit There is no talent shortage. There is a relevance shortage. When 82% employers struggle to hire, it means: • Skills taught are outdated. • Students lack applied exposure. • Faculty-industry disconnect is widening. • Soft skills deficit is real. • Technology adoption in curriculum is slow. And most importantly: Learning has become transactional. Not transformational. Why This Matters More Than You Think If India cannot align education with industry: • Productivity drops. • Startups suffer. • Global competitiveness weakens. • Youth frustration rises. Demographic dividend can easily become demographic disaster. And this is not theory. It is already visible. The Real Question: Who Will Fix This? Government alone cannot. Universities alone cannot. Corporates alone cannot. This requires a new learning ecosystem: 1. Industry-integrated curriculum 2. Real-time skill mapping 3. Project-based evaluation 4. AI-powered learning personalization 5. Mentorship + accountability Learning must move from: Syllabus-driven → Market-driven Theory-heavy → Application-heavy Degree-focused → Skill-certified What Students Must Understand Today Your degree is not your leverage. Your problem-solving ability is. Your ability to: • Build • Analyze • Communicate • Adapt • Learn fast That is currency. The job market has evolved. If you don’t evolve, you get eliminated. A Hard Truth for Parents Stop asking: “Beta, degree ho gaya?” Start asking: “Beta, skill kya hai?” A Harder Truth for Institutions Placement percentage is not impact. Sustained employability is. If students are not job-ready on Day 1, we have failed them. The India We Need India does not need more graduates. India needs: • Cloud engineers • AI operators • Data storytellers • Cybersecurity analysts • Automation architects • Industry-ready professionals And above all — Self-driven lifelong learners. The Future Belongs to Learning Machines & Learning Minds Technology is not replacing jobs. Unskilled professionals are being replaced by skilled professionals who use technology. That’s the shift. #IndiaSkills #TalentCrisis #NewEducation #IndustryReady 5 2 Comments Like Comment Share Copy LinkedIn Facebook X To view or add a comment, sign in

Chandra Shekhar yadav 1mo Report this post AGI: Can India turn disruption into opportunity? A thought-provoking question from today’s The Pioneer: If Artificial General Intelligence is as close as many experts suggest, is India preparing for the disruption—or only dreaming about the opportunity? The bigger question is not “Will AI take jobs?” It is: What happens when AI can perform increasingly complex cognitive work—not just repetitive tasks? India has a unique position in this transition. We have: A massive young workforce One of the world's largest pools of engineers and knowledge workers A rapidly expanding digital economy Millions entering the workforce every year But we also have a vulnerability: A large part of our employment advantage has historically come from supplying human cognitive labour at scale. If AI can increasingly provide that cognitive labour at a fraction of the cost, the equation changes. And this is where the opportunity lies. The real race is not AI vs humans. It is humans + AI vs humans without AI. A doctor using AI can potentially diagnose more effectively. A teacher can personalise learning for hundreds of students. A lawyer can analyse enormous volumes of documents. A small business can access capabilities that once required an entire team. A student can have a personalised tutor, career coach and research assistant. But there is a second side to this story. AI will not eliminate the need for human capability. It will redefine what capability means. Knowing how to use AI will increasingly become table stakes. The premium will move towards: Judgement + domain expertise + creativity + communication + problem-solving + AI fluency. And that creates a serious question for India: Are our schools and universities preparing young people for AI-assisted work— or are we still preparing them for a world where knowledge itself is the competitive advantage? Because knowledge is becoming cheaper. Judgement isn't. Information is becoming abundant. The ability to ask the right question isn't. Execution is becoming automated. Knowing what should be executed—and why—is becoming more valuable. Food for thought: If a 15-year-old today will enter the workforce around 2035... What exactly should we be teaching them? And if a large percentage of today's white-collar jobs are transformed rather than simply destroyed... Are we preparing young people to compete for jobs—or to work alongside intelligent machines? India's AGI opportunity may ultimately depend less on whether we build the world's best AI model... and much more on whether we build the world's most AI-capable population. The future of work is not just an AI question. It is an education question. A skills question. A leadership question. And ultimately, a national competitiveness question. What do you think? Chandra Shekhar yadav 2mo Report this post Seeds for the 1st layer of transformation of education. And perhaps, a lot more is in the pipeline. The announcements from the Red Fort on free online coaching for competitive examinations and AI-skilling of 1 crore young Indians in the coming year deserve attention—not just as government schemes, but as signals of where Indian education could be heading. (PM India) For decades, access to quality coaching has been deeply unequal. The student with resources could access the best teachers, coaching centres and learning ecosystems. The student without them often had talent—but not the same opportunity. A nationwide digital coaching ecosystem can potentially change that equation. And the AI-skilling target is equally significant. Education is slowly moving from “access to content” towards “access to capability”. But this is only the beginning. The real transformation will depend on execution. Some difficult questions need to be answered: → Will free online coaching provide quality, or merely content? → How will we address the digital divide and students with weak devices/connectivity? → Who will provide mentorship, doubt resolution, assessment and personalised learning? → Can online systems reach students who struggle with language, foundational literacy or self-discipline? → Most importantly, will AI training mean merely using AI tools, or actually developing AI literacy, critical thinking, problem-solving and employability? Because 1 crore trained is a number. 1 crore capable is a transformation. India has the opportunity to build something much bigger than another online education platform—a public digital learning ecosystem that combines teachers + technology + AI + assessment + mentorship + career pathways. The seeds are being planted. The first layer is access. The next layers must be quality, equity, capability and outcomes. And if this is indeed just the first layer, I am curious to see what comes next. The transformation of Indian education may have just entered a new phase. #Education #AI #SkillDevelopment #FutureOfWork #EdTech #ArtificialIntelligence #DigitalIndia #Youth #EducationReform #India Like Comment Share Copy LinkedIn Facebook X To view or add a comment, sign in
